 Serbia and Germany meet in the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 on Friday, 13 November, at 19:45 GMT. The fixture takes place at the Rajko Mitić Stadium in Belgrade, with Germany chasing a vital victory in League A, Group 2.
 The visitors won the reverse fixture 2-0 in October and remain in contention for a quarter-final place. Serbia, meanwhile, have lost all four group matches and are looking to avoid another defeat against one of Europe’s strongest national teams.
 Keep reading to discover our betting tips and analysis for this exciting encounter.

 Serbia vs. Germany - Head-to-head record
 Serbia and Germany have met three times since Serbia began competing independently, with each nation recording one victory alongside a draw.
 Their most famous encounter came during the 2010 World Cup, when Serbia secured a surprise 1-0 victory over Germany. Milan Jovanović scored the decisive goal in a match that also saw Miroslav Klose dismissed.
 The teams met again in March 2019, playing out a 1-1 friendly draw. Luka Jović gave Serbia an early lead before Leon Goretzka equalised for Germany.
 Their latest meeting came on 1 October 2026, when Germany recorded a 2-0 Nations League victory . That result demonstrated the difference between the sides’ current performances, with Germany controlling the match and keeping Serbia’s attack quiet.
 Germany now have an opportunity to complete a group-stage double, while Serbia will hope home advantage can help them produce another upset.
 Serbia - Looking to end their losing streak
 Serbia enter Friday’s fixture at the bottom of Nations League Group A2, having failed to collect a point from their opening four matches. Veljko Paunović’s side need a significant improvement to challenge Germany.
 Recent form
 Serbia have endured a difficult Nations League campaign, losing all four matches against Greece, the Netherlands and Germany.
 They began with consecutive 2-1 defeats against Greece and the Netherlands. Germany then secured a 2-0 victory in October before Serbia suffered another 2-1 loss against the Netherlands.
 Their defensive performances have been a recurring problem. Serbia have conceded in every group match, while their attack has struggled to create enough opportunities to compensate.
 There is some encouragement in the return of Aleksandar Mitrović and Dušan Vlahović to the national squad. Both forwards missed the September and October international windows, and their availability provides Serbia with additional attacking options.
 However, midfield suspensions create another challenge. Saša Lukić and Nemanja Maksimović are unavailable, while Aleksandar Stanković and Aleksa Terzić are sidelined.
 Serbia will need to improve their defensive organisation and make better use of possession. With Germany expected to control midfield, counterattacks and set pieces could provide the hosts with their best opportunities.

 Injuries and selection: Aleksandar Stanković is unavailable with an adductor injury, while Aleksa Terzić is also sidelined. Strahinja Pavlović is a fitness concern. Mitrović and Vlahović have returned to the squad.
 Germany - Looking to close the gap on the leaders
 Germany travel to Belgrade knowing that victory is essential to their Nations League quarter-final ambitions. Jürgen Klopp’s side sit third in Group A2, three points behind the Netherlands and Greece.
 Recent form
 Germany have experienced an inconsistent start to their Nations League campaign, collecting five points from four matches.
 They opened with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands before suffering a disappointing 1-0 home defeat to Greece. Their first victory came against Serbia in October, when they secured a 2-0 win.
 A goalless draw away to Greece followed, leaving Germany with just three goals scored across their opening four group matches.
 Their defensive record has been considerably stronger. Germany have conceded only twice in the competition and kept clean sheets in their last two matches.
 Florian Wirtz remains one of their most important attacking players, providing creativity between midfield and attack. Kai Havertz offers movement and versatility up front, while Joshua Kimmich plays a central role in controlling possession.
 Germany’s biggest challenge is converting their possession into goals. Against a Serbia side that have conceded in every group match, Klopp will expect a more productive attacking performance.

 Serbia vs. Germany - Stats
 Serbia have lost all four of their Nations League matches, scoring three goals and conceding eight.
 Three of Serbia’s four group defeats have ended 2-1.
 Serbia have conceded at least twice in every Nations League match this season.
 Germany have won one, drawn two and lost one of their four group matches.
 Germany have conceded just two goals in four Nations League fixtures.
 Germany defeated Serbia 2-0 in their previous meeting on 1 October 2026.
 Germany are unbeaten in their last nine away Nations League matches.
 Predictions for Serbia vs. Germany - Germany tipped for victory
 Germany enter this fixture as clear favourites, having already beaten Serbia 2-0 in October. Their defensive record gives them an advantage against a Serbian side that have struggled throughout the competition.
 Serbia have conceded at least twice in every Nations League match, making a decisive result and over 2.5 goals an appealing selection. Germany’s need for three points should encourage an attacking approach, particularly with goal difference potentially influencing qualification.
 A Serbia victory would represent a significant upset. However, the return of Mitrović and Vlahović gives the hosts more attacking options than they had in the reverse fixture. Backing Serbia to win with over 1.5 goals offers a higher-risk alternative for those expecting a surprise result.
 Our main prediction is for Germany to win. Their stronger defensive performances, midfield quality and previous victory over Serbia make them the more convincing choice.
